key_insight: VGGT-Edit enables native, feed-forward 3D scene editing by predicting a residual field that modifies an existing neural scene representation in a single pass, producing consistent multi-view edits without per-view optimization.
problem_solved: Existing editing pipelines edit 2D views independently or require iterative optimization, leading to multi-view inconsistency, slow turnaround, and poor interactivity. This work addresses the need for fast, coherent, instruction-driven edits directly in 3D.
method: Feed-forward residual field prediction: infer a 3D delta field that warps or updates a base neural scene representation to apply edits in one forward pass.
Operate natively in 3D (not 2D lift-and-project): ensures multi-view and geometry consistency by applying edits in the scene’s volumetric/neural field coordinate frame.
Lightweight integration with existing reconstruction models: produces real-time or near-real-time edits while preserving scene fidelity.
impact: Provides interactive, consistent 3D editing suitable for AR/VR, content creation, and human-in-the-loop workflows, enabling faster prototyping and deployment of editable neural scenes. Practitioners gain a practical path from static reconstruction to responsive, instruction-driven scene manipulation.

paper_title: VGGT-Edit: Feed-forward Native 3D Scene Editing with Residual Field Prediction
paper_authors: Kaixin Zhu, Yiwen Tang, Yifan Yang, Renrui Zhang, Bohan Zeng
